summary: US-005: QR e-ticket issued and delivered
description:
**As** a buyer, **I want** my ticket with a QR code by email and on a web page after purchase. Mailer is a port with log transport (brief non-goal: no notifications service).

**Priority:** P1
**Depends on:** US-004 (TKT-28)

**Acceptance Criteria:**
- [ ] Access service issues a signed QR payload per paid ticket, triggered by the order-completed event
- [ ] Mailer port (log transport) records a delivery with ticket link; buyer ticket page renders the QR (browser-verified)
- [ ] Issuance and delivery are recorded as append-only ticket lifecycle events linked to the order (ADR-003); the ticket's history is queryable; lifecycle events carry pseudonymous IDs only — delivery address resolved from the PII store at send time
- [ ] Tickets are re-retrievable by order reference (guest flow, no account)

Quality gates: `make check` green (defined in US-001, mirrors CI); contract tests for touched service boundaries; UI: browser-verified with screenshot in PR; money paths: NF525 journal chain verifies (from US-004).

binding.rule: We build five Go services (catalog, inventory, commerce, payments, access) behind an API gateway, with an event bus for the domain event stream; every entity carries a tenant/organizer id from day one. Docker Compose only.

Append-only trails, one discipline: (1) money journal — every money-relevant record immutable, sequence-numbered, hash-chained, signed; corrections are compensating entries; read models are projections; verify-journal in the local gate from US-004. (2) ticket lifecycle trace — every ticket/entitlement state change is an append-only lifecycle event linked to its order; redemption/reissue decisions are made from the trace. (3) trails are pseudonymous: records reference customers by pseudonymous ID only, PII lives in a separate erasable store; no raw PII in any append-only record (enforced invariant from US-004). (4) NF525 is a later-phase profile that must layer on without schema or flow changes.

comments.body: Scope amended pre-Gate-1 (owner directive 2026-07-12): NF525 is NOT an immediate goal — it becomes a later-phase French-market profile. The underlying requirement is generalized: traceability is a must, with the same audit-trail thinking for money AND tickets (ADR-003 reworked accordingly). New AC: issuance/delivery recorded as append-only lifecycle events.
Backlog grilling 2026-07-12 (owner decisions): lifecycle events pseudonymous per amended ADR-003.

Claimed after owner acceptance of TKT-28 (2026-07-13). TKT-29 is the next unblocked walking-skeleton story and P1 dependency for TKT-30. It will establish the access-service issuance/delivery boundary, with pseudonymous lifecycle events per ADR-003; plan review applies.

<!-- sdlc:stage=planning kind=plan -->
## Draft execution plan — TKT-29 / US-005

**Branch:** `TKT-29-ticket-delivery` from `origin/main` at `a553380` after Gate 2 approval.

**Definition of done:** a completed Commerce order produces exactly one signed QR ticket per reserved quantity in Access, an append-only and pseudonymous `issued → delivered` lifecycle trace, a log-transport delivery with a guest retrieval link, and a browser-rendered QR ticket page. The primary Compose smoke seam starts at the public Commerce checkout route and observes the result only through public Access/gateway surfaces plus the lifecycle trace. `payments verify-journal` remains in the smoke gate.

### Decision proposed — ADR-012: ticket issuance, lifecycle, and QR token boundary

- **Access owns tickets, lifecycle events, QR credentials, and delivery attempts.** Commerce remains owner of orders and erasable buyer PII. Access never persists or logs a name/email.
- **Event contract:** after an order is durably completed, Commerce publishes the ADR-009 envelope on `platform.commerce.order.completed`, schema 1. Its minimal data is `order_id`, `organizer_id`, `buyer_id`, `slot_id`, `ticket_type_id`, and `quantity`—identifiers only, no money or PII. Publication is acknowledged by JetStream and deterministic by order ID. Access uses a durable consumer with an inbox/idempotency record; redelivery or checkout replay cannot create extra tickets.
- **Current reliability frontier:** Commerce will retry publication on the checkout replay path, but a crash after completion with no retry can delay issuance. Scheduled/restart outbox draining remains intentionally owned by TKT-43; this story must not silently claim it has solved that crash boundary.
- **QR token:** per ticket, Access produces a compact, versioned Ed25519-signed payload containing only ticket UUID, organizer/slot IDs, issuance time, and `kid`; it contains no PII, money, or mutable admission state. Access stores the canonical payload and serves it as QR artwork. The private key is injected configuration, never stored in the database or logs; `kid` makes later key rotation and TKT-30 verification possible.
- **Trace and delivery:** in the Access transaction, persist the ticket and immutable `issued` event; after the log-mail port accepts a deterministic message ID, append immutable `delivered`. Delivery resolves email from a token-protected Commerce internal PII endpoint only at send time. The log transport records delivery ID, ticket/order references, recipient hash, and ticket link—not raw email. Database guards deny UPDATE/DELETE/TRUNCATE of lifecycle rows.
- **Guest retrieval:** an unguessable UUID order reference is returned by the completed checkout response and used for `GET /orders/{order_ref}/tickets` and the localized `/[locale]/tickets/[order_ref]` page. These are `Cache-Control: no-store` personal reads. Account wallet, PDF, rotating codes, real email, reissue, and scanning remain out of scope.

### Implementation sequence

1. Write ADR-012 and contract-first OpenAPI documents before handlers: Access public ticket bundle/history and QR-artwork endpoints, Commerce’s completed-order response plus token-protected internal delivery-address endpoint. Add generation/served-spec/drift coverage per ADR-009 and register only the public Access routes through the gateway.
2. Add Commerce migration/API changes to expose an order reference only after completed checkout, look up delivery email internally by pseudonymous buyer ID, and publish the deterministic schema-1 completed-order envelope with JetStream acknowledgement on successful completion/replay. Do not put PII into the event, Commerce facts, or logs.
3. Add Access migrations and store: inbox de-duplication, tickets, immutable lifecycle events, and delivery-attempt records. The transaction atomically consumes one event and creates `quantity` tickets plus one `issued` event each; it is safe for duplicate messages and concurrent consumer delivery.
4. Add Access’s durable JetStream consumer and delivery dispatcher. The dispatcher resolves recipient PII through Commerce using `X-Internal-Token`, invokes a port with deterministic delivery/message ID, and appends `delivered` exactly once after acceptance. Implement the local log transport with recipient hashing/redaction and no email persistence. Wire service token, Commerce URL, and QR signing configuration through Compose and smoke variants.
5. Implement the QR signer/validator and image endpoint using the versioned `kid` payload; reject malformed, forged, unknown-key, and mismatched ticket requests. Keep admission/redeem logic out of this ticket for TKT-30.
6. Add the Astro ticket page and checkout success hand-off: localised confirmation links to `/en|fr/tickets/{order_ref}`, the page makes one no-store Access bundle call, and a small QR renderer renders the signed payload. Extend the reproducible Playwright script to checkout, follow the guest link, assert an actual QR element and rendered lifecycle, and write evidence under `docs/verification/ticket-delivery/`.
7. Tests first at each seam: QR signing/tampering/key-ID tests; Access transaction, quantity, duplicate/redelivery/concurrency, lifecycle guard/history, and PII no-leak tests; Commerce event/PII internal-auth tests; mail-port redaction/idempotency tests; request/response and served-spec contract tests; Compose smoke checkout→delivery→guest retrieval/replay tests. Keep `verify-journal` in the smoke lifecycle, then run `make check`.
8. Update architecture, configuration, development/testing docs and the system diagram with the Commerce→JetStream→Access→ephemeral-PII lookup flow; retain the explicit TKT-43 recovery limitation.

### Pre-mortem

Likely failure modes are duplicate tickets from JetStream redelivery, a stale/forged QR being treated as valid, email crossing an append-only or log boundary, and a completed order losing issuance at the Commerce publish boundary. The plan prevents the first three with Access inbox/unique lifecycle facts, Ed25519+`kid` validation, and an ephemeral PII lookup/redacted transport. The fourth is explicitly bounded to retry-driven issuance in this walking skeleton and remains TKT-43’s outbox/restart-recovery work.

### Approval requested at Gate 2

Approve ADR-012’s ownership and Ed25519 QR format, the guest order-reference capability route, and the explicit TKT-43 publication-recovery boundary. No code will begin until this plan is approved.

## Gate-2 plan amendment — review corrections accepted

This amendment supersedes the draft plan where it conflicts; all other scope, tests, and the explicit TKT-43 recovery boundary remain unchanged.

1. **Commerce publishing is net-new work in this ticket.** `s.fact(..., "order.completed")` currently writes a local Commerce fact and appends the payment journal; it does **not** publish to JetStream. TKT-29 introduces Commerce’s first domain-event publisher, its `platform.commerce.order.completed` schema-1 contract, deterministic event ID/NATS `Nats-Msg-Id`, unit tests, and a Compose smoke contract. Access consumes this new event; it is not an existing seam.

2. **Completion commit precedes publication.** The event is constructed from the authoritative reservation/order data but is published only after the transaction that writes `reservations.status=completed`, `orders.status=completed`, and the guest reference has committed successfully. A failure before that commit emits nothing. An acknowledged JetStream publish failure returns a retryable response; a replay of an already-completed checkout calls `ensureCompletedPublished` before returning success. This yields at-least-once delivery without issuing a ticket for a rolled-back completion. A crash after commit before publish can still delay issuance until a checkout retry—precisely the publication gap retained for TKT-43’s transactional outbox/restart recovery, not a claim this story hides.

3. **Guest retrieval uses a separate random capability, never `order_id`.** Add a nullable-until-success `guest_order_ref` to Commerce orders; mint it with CSPRNG-backed UUIDv4 inside the successful completion transaction, enforce uniqueness, and return it only in the completed response. The schema-1 event carries it so Access can index the ticket bundle. The no-store guest endpoints and localized ticket page use only this opaque reference; they do not treat the deterministic SHA-1 order ID as a bearer credential. No capability is written to structured logs, lifecycle payloads, mail transport logs, or the money journal.

4. **Strengthen idempotency details.** The event’s `quantity` is the authoritative completed reservation quantity. Access’s inbox uniqueness is keyed on envelope event ID (not order ID) and the ticket/lifecycle uniqueness makes duplicate or concurrent delivery harmless. `issued` is unique per issued ticket; `delivered` has a database uniqueness constraint on `(ticket_id, event_type)` (or its deterministic lifecycle-event ID), so a redelivered JetStream message or retried dispatcher cannot append delivery twice. The deterministic mail message ID gives the log port the same retry safety across send/append crash boundaries.

5. **Signing configuration is end-to-end.** `ACCESS_QR_PRIVATE_KEY` and active `ACCESS_QR_KID` are required at Access startup and wired in both `compose.yaml` and `compose.smoke.yaml`; tests construct a separate keypair and cover valid, forged, unknown-`kid`, and ticket/payload mismatch cases. Only public verification material is usable in TKT-30; private signing material is never logged or persisted.

**Revised approval request:** approve the amended plan and ADR-012 with (a) new Commerce publisher, (b) post-commit retry-driven publication only pending TKT-43, (c) CSPRNG guest capability references, and (d) explicit ticket/delivery idempotency constraints. No code has begun.

objective.note: US-005 acceptance criteria specify signed QR issuance, log delivery, pseudonymous lifecycle trace, and guest re-retrieval.

scope.note: In: access issuance, delivery port/log transport, ticket/history and guest retrieval surfaces, Commerce event/PII seam, storefront ticket page, contracts/tests/evidence. Out: accounts wallet, rotating barcodes/PDF/real email (TKT-18), scanner behavior (TKT-30).

uncertainties.note: Delivery-event reliability, QR signing/key lifecycle, and safe PII lookup are design decisions to resolve and record during planning; no external dependency blocks them.

dependencies.note: TKT-28 is Done; PR #7 established the order-completed event, pseudonymous buyer correlation, separate Commerce PII store, and verified journal.

approach.note: Contract-first and event-driven: consume completed orders idempotently, issue opaque signed ticket QR payloads, append immutable lifecycle events, resolve PII only at mail-send boundary.

first_slice.note: One coherent vertical slice: completed checkout produces a retrievable QR ticket and log-mail delivery, verified through gateway/browser and lifecycle history.

success.note: All US-005 ACs, contracts, browser screenshot, populated journal verification, and make check green.
